qc.label_under_test: A second, mirrored labelling clause that casts the narrator: after one clause casts someone as something (sees him as a hero, calls her a liar), a following clause casts me or us (and she sees me as a nuisance, they treat us as outsiders); it fires on the 'as' or 'a' right after 'me'/'us', whoever does the labelling and whether or not the label is handed back. The same second clause aimed at him, her, you or them is weak, as is a one-way label of me with no earlier labelling clause, or me labelled in the first clause and answering back. Strongest when a sentence of setting comes first.

neighbours.label: A second, mirrored labelling clause that casts the narrator: after one clause casts someone as something (sees him as a hero, calls her a liar), a following clause casts me or us (and she sees me as a nuisance, they treat us as outsiders); it fires on the 'as' or 'a' right after 'me'/'us', whoever does the labelling and whether or not the label is handed back. The same second clause aimed at him, her, you or them is weak, as is a one-way label of me with no earlier labelling clause, or me labelled in the first clause and answering back. Strongest when a sentence of setting comes first.
fire: The office was quiet after lunch. My boss sees Daniel as a rising star, and she sees me as a nuisance.
Rain hammered the windows of the old farmhouse. Grandpa called my cousin a genius, then he called me a dreamer.
The village had only one pub. The locals treat the vicar as family, but they treat us as outsiders.
It was the first week of term. The teacher saw Priya as a leader and saw me as a troublemaker.
Snow had closed the mountain pass for days. The guide regarded the climbers as amateurs, and he regarded us as dead weight.
The kitchen smelled of burnt toast. Mom thinks my brother is a saint, and she thinks of me as a lost cause.
Our band played the small club every Friday. The owner billed the drummer as the star and billed us as the warm-up act.
The courtroom was packed that morning. The prosecutor painted the witness as a liar, and the jury saw me as an accomplice.
quiet: The office was quiet after lunch. My boss sees Daniel as a rising star, and she sees him as a future partner.
Rain hammered the windows of the old farmhouse. Grandpa called my cousin a genius, then he called her a dreamer.
The village had only one pub. The locals treat the vicar as family, but they treat them as outsiders.
It was the first week of term. The teacher saw me as a troublemaker, and I saw her as a tyrant.
Snow had closed the mountain pass for days. The guide regarded us as dead weight.
The kitchen smelled of burnt toast. Mom thinks my brother is a saint, and she gave me a slice of toast.
Our band played the small club every Friday. The owner billed the drummer as the star and billed you as the warm-up act.
The courtroom was packed that morning. The jury saw me as an accomplice, so I called the prosecutor a liar.

predictions: Confirm expected: probes put mirrored me/us clauses at 0.19-0.46 and you/them or one-way me under 0.07; the neighbour reading (any verb+object+as/to slot) stayed under 0.05.
